links.speaker: Fatima
links.quote: I can do that.

links.speaker: Ravi
links.quote: The fourth floor gets the Tessaline felt panels, I'll put that in the note to finance today.

links.speaker: Henrik
links.quote: That's fair, actually.

links.speaker: Ravi
links.quote: Good thought, I'll drop her a line. The training's the thirtieth, half a day.

links.speaker: Ravi
links.quote: Fatima, you've got the permit list. Dmitri, the Tessaline paperwork. I've got the lift, and I'm late for the fire people.

links.speaker: Ravi
links.quote: Then reopen it, Dmitri, I can't fix it from here.

links.speaker: Kwame
links.quote: Did anyone actually look at it, or did they just close the ticket?

links.speaker: Ravi
links.quote: Reopen it. Fatima, the permit list?

links.speaker: Ravi
links.quote: 36 against 44 requests, then. Thanks. Parked till April anyway.

links.speaker: Ravi
links.quote: I've asked him. Kwame, the Christmas invoice?

links.speaker: Ravi
links.quote: Good thing you checked. I'll pay it. Who signed for the hour?

links.speaker: Ravi
links.quote: So the third of February holds.

links.speaker: Henrik
links.quote: It ends with me paying sixty pounds for a new hatch, so, sort of, yes.

links.speaker: Dmitri
links.quote: So that's the end of the month. We can't sit on it till then, the order has to go by the twenty-fourth or we lose the slot-

links.speaker: Dmitri
links.quote: Yeah, I can do that today. I'd also like to ask Tessaline what the C actually means, whether it's the test or whether-

links.speaker: Ravi
links.quote: In writing, same as the lead time. Fatima, can you get hold of the surveyor before his report's out? Even an email, just with the exact wording.

links.speaker: Ravi
links.quote: Nothing changes on paper yet. It's still the Tessaline felt, finance has it, I just want to see those three answers before we talk about it again.

links.speaker: Ravi
links.quote: It's in my inbox, Kwame, I know where it is. We'll come back to it.

links.speaker: Ravi
links.quote: Log it, Henrik. Same as the machine.

links.speaker: Dmitri
links.quote: Speaking of which, I'm going to go and reopen 4417.

links.speaker: Ravi
links.quote: Do. Fatima, you'll send me whatever you get from him?

links.speaker: Ravi
links.quote: Fine, I'll warn the cleaners. Right. The panel order. Tessaline have answered on the corridor rating, so I want that back open, properly, before my name goes on anything.

links.speaker: Ravi
links.quote: Legal came back Wednesday. It's one policy, whole building, and there's a condition that escape routes are kept to whatever standard the insurer's surveyor sets. Breach it and they can decline a claim.

links.speaker: Dmitri
links.quote: That's the thing, they've got it, it's in the email, if the order's in today it comes on the same delivery. So it doesn't touch the fitters.

links.speaker: Ravi
links.quote: Hang on, though. Can I hear the other side of it first. Is there an argument for leaving the order exactly as it stands?

links.speaker: Henrik
links.quote: And it's just the 46 metres of corridor that goes over to their mineral-wool-core panel, the B-s1,d0 one, 3,800 pounds, and we still make the third of February, and that's the whole cost of not having this conversation with an insurer.

links.speaker: Henrik
links.quote: No, that's it, that's me. I just don't see tearing up the floor for it.

links.speaker: Ravi
links.quote: 19,220 plus 3,800 is 23,020 before fixing. The slat quote was 24,025. So we're still under that by 1,005.

links.speaker: Ravi
links.quote: Okay. Tessaline felt stays across the floor, and the 46 square metres of escape corridor get the mineral-wool-core panel at B-s1,d0.

links.speaker: Ravi
links.quote: And I'll write to finance today for the extra 3,800, with the surveyor's email and the certificate attached. Fatima, can you send me his?

links.speaker: Ravi
links.quote: Cleaning contract's on the thirty-first, ten o'clock. 41,600, up 6 percent. Who's got the complaints log?

links.speaker: Ravi
links.quote: Bring that on the thirty-first, then. That's it, I've got the bins to sort out.
